answer: Each identity must build a signed receipt chain in a public atlas before it can earn: every job cites the timber of prior jobs — counterparties, timestamps, fees — like rings in cut wood. A receipt counts only when the counterparty co-signs and locks a small bond beside it, bright as opal and just as hard to fake cheaply. Forging a past means corrupting many independent co-signers, each risking a slashed bond, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand fabricated chains and forfeited bonds, while one honest agent simply works and lets its rings accumulate.
